Not repaired. The failure is an access/renderability failure of the publisher's terms document, not a missing or wrong licence. I re-verified that https://clinicaltrials.gov/about-site/terms-conditions is a client-side-rendered single-page app: a raw, non-JS capture of that URL (confirmed via the Internet Archive raw snapshot https://web.archive.org/web/20260101010541id_/https://clinicaltrials.gov/about-site/terms-conditions) returns only the glossary shell ("Hide glossary ... Search for terms") and contains none of the Terms text, including "Attribute the source of the data as ClinicalTrials.gov". That is exactly why the worker's capture contained no such excerpt, and re-supplying a different quote against the same SPA URL would not repair it (a headless/proxy render such as my extraction tool seeing the text does not mean the worker's plain fetch can). No accessible official alternative was found that reproduces this specific ClinicalTrials.gov terms document: NLM's own static terms pages (https://www.nlm.nih.gov/databases/download/terms_and_conditions.html and https://www.nlm.nih.gov/databases/download.html) are generic NLM data-distribution terms that do not name or apply to ClinicalTrials.gov records, and the NLM Data Distribution programme page lists only MEDLINE/PubMed, MeSH and Catalog data — using them would commit the precise error the task forbids (a generic licence page does not establish that this publisher applied those terms to these data). The only exact reproductions of the ClinicalTrials.gov terms text outside the SPA are non-official third-party copies (a GitHub LICENSE file, PubChem's own JS-rendered source page, judicial PDFs), which cannot serve as the terms_url. Separately, the official API documentation page https://clinicaltrials.gov/data-api/about-api/study-data-structure is likewise an SPA; the machine-readable OpenAPI specification is accessible and static at https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/oas/v2, but it documents endpoints and schemas only and carries no rights statement, and the .yaml variant (/api/oas/v2/ctg-oas-v2.yaml) returns 404. On the substantive law, the position is also not a clean statutory public-domain grant: 17 U.S.C. §105 removes U.S. copyright only from works of the U.S. Government, these records are submitted by sponsors and institutions, the publisher states that some data may be subject to third-party copyright, and the publisher asserts an international copyright outside the United States and its Territories or Possessions. So neither an invented worldwide dedication nor a blanket government-domain claim is supportable. Because readable, capturable, publisher-applicable compatible terms could not be established for these specific records, the correct outcome is defer rather than a fabricated terms_excerpt or a substituted generic licence page. The existing non-terms evidence (the two API count checks: 105,978 COMPLETED and 13,817 TERMINATED; the live record-shape and status-filter checks) is API JSON served by a non-SPA endpoint and remains valid and untouched; the dataset, download URLs, prediction task, features and split policy are unchanged.

No candidate survived verification as a ready, no-account, label-complete source in this pass. (1) USPTO Trademark Case Files Dataset was the strongest task design (filing-time prediction of registration within N months, 12.7M cases, documented 79-field schema), but every bulk file is now served through the USPTO Open Data Portal, which since 18 June 2026 requires a signed-in USPTO.gov account with MFA ('In order to access the Open Data Portal (ODP), starting on June 18, 2026, you'll need to sign in with a valid USPTO.gov account'), and the case-files page states downloads now resolve through ODP signed URLs. That is an account-gated source, which the brief excludes. (2) The UK Companies House Free Company Data Product is no-account, single-file (471 MB ZIP, documented 40-field CSV including Dissolution Date and Incorporation Date), but it holds only companies still on the register: independent field profiling of a 99,999-row release slice reports 'DissolutionDate is 0% populated across all 99,999 records', and the publisher describes the snapshot as 'basic company data of live companies on the register'. With dissolved companies absent, no survival/dissolution label can be constructed, so the file cannot support the target. (3) The Charity Commission for England and Wales register extract remains promising and is the fallback worth resuming: it contains removed as well as registered charities and documents date_of_registration and date_of_removal ('For non-removed charities the field is NULL'), but I could not in this pass confirm the publisher's current licence designation for the extract as a whole, the exact stable download URLs, or the per-table fields needed for filing-time features (charitable purposes, area of operation, charity type). Those must be read before freezing a task.

Two candidate sources were researched to the level of a real download, documentation and terms, and both fail one required condition. (1) The FAA National Wildlife Strike Database is the best task fit (independent strike reports since 1990, ~344k rows, rich pre-outcome circumstance fields, ICAO damage definitions in the published field list at https://wildlife.faa.gov/assets/fieldlist.pdf), but on the current site the bulk export is only reachable through an interactive 'Search the Database' form (https://wildlife.faa.gov/search) that redirects anonymous fetches to /home; the only documented programmatic interface (wildlife.faa.gov/api) is credential-gated for strike submission, and no verified anonymous file URL (e.g. the often-cited wildlife.faa.gov/downloads/wildlife_data.csv, which is only asserted by third-party GitHub pages) could be confirmed. The records are also third-party strike reports compiled by USDA/WS under an interagency agreement, so an unqualified public-domain claim would need more legal evidence than a .gov domain. (2) The NTSB Census of US Civil Aviation Accidents is fully verifiable — direct file https://data.ntsb.gov/avdata/FileDirectory/DownloadFile?fileID=avall.zip (97,140,358 bytes, created 11/1/2026), schema https://data.ntsb.gov/avdata/FileDirectory/DownloadFile?fileID=eadmspub.pdf, dictionary https://www.ntsb.gov/Pages/AviationDownloadDataDictionary.aspx, 17 U.S.C. 105 https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap1.html#105 — but the only substantive binary label (fatal vs non-fatal, ev_highest_injury/inj_tot_f, defined by death within 30 days per 49 CFR 830.2) duplicates the already-selected Great Britain collision-severity task almost exactly, and every other defensible label in that file (damage class, fire/explosion, findings, probable cause) is a post-investigation determination, so the family adds little beyond an existing item. Rather than force one of these two through, the honest call is to defer and pick a source that is both anonymous-bulk-downloadable and not a severity-of-the-same-event rerun.
